intro: Searching for a company accountant near you usually means you run or help run a limited company and want someone local who can take care of the statutory accounts, corporation tax returns and confirmation statements. You may be setting up a new company, changing accountants, or simply feeling that filing deadlines are creeping up on you. iComply is a free introduction service: you tell us what you need, and we introduce you to a suitable UK accountant who quotes you directly, with quotes on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a company accountant near me usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search want a local accountant who understands the duties of a company director, not just personal tax.
needs: You have formed a limited company and need statutory accounts, a corporation tax return and a confirmation statement prepared and filed on time.
You are a director who wants clear advice on salary, dividends and expenses so you can pay yourself sensibly and keep records straight.
You are leaving your current accountant and want someone nearby who can take over the company's records without disruption.
You want to know whether payroll and VAT will be handled as part of the service, or whether those are separate arrangements.
You would like a local professional you can sit down with, ask questions of, and rely on to track filing deadlines with you.
context_heading: What to understand about the word accountant
context: In the UK the word "accountant" on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can use it. Titles such as Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, and members are bound by their body's ethics, training and complaints rules. Only registered auditors can sign statutory audit reports, so if you are ever told you need an audit, ask who will sign it.

Every practice offering accountancy services must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. It is reasonable to ask which body supervises a firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled. Searching for a company accountant near me is a good starting point, but these questions help you judge what you find.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say whether your company is already trading, newly formed or dormant, so the accountant knows what filings are likely to be needed.

Explain whether payroll and VAT are part of what you want handled, or whether those are already covered elsewhere.
Tell us roughly where you are based and how far you are willing to travel, since you searched for a company accountant near me.
Note whether you are moving from another accountant, and whether there is any unfinished filing you are worried about.
Include anything unusual about the company, such as several directors, a change of year end, or income from outside the UK.
questions: Which body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Do you hold a protected title such as Chartered Accountant or Chartered Certified Accountant, and which body are you a member of?
Will you prepare the statutory accounts, corporation tax return and confirmation statement, and who tracks the filing deadlines?
Can you advise on director salary, dividends and expenses, and how is that advice provided?
Are payroll and VAT included in what you offer, or are they arranged separately?
How do you handle complaints, and what is your process for taking over records from a previous accountant?

faqs.q: Do I legally need an accountant for my limited company?
faqs.a: Directors are responsible for keeping proper records and filing statutory accounts, a corporation tax return and a confirmation statement on time. Many directors use a company accountant to prepare and file these, but the legal duties remain with the directors.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an accountant and a registered auditor?
faqs.a: An accountant prepares accounts and tax returns, while only a registered auditor can sign statutory audit reports. Most small companies are not required to be audited, but if you are told you need one, ask who will sign the report.

faqs.q: How can I check an accountant's credentials?
faqs.a: Ask which professional body they belong to and which body supervises the practice for anti-money-laundering purposes. Protected titles such as Chartered Accountant and Chartered Certified Accountant mean the member is bound by that body's ethics, training and complaints rules.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I speak to a company accountant?
faqs.a: It helps to have your company registration details, recent bank statements, records of income and expenses, and any correspondence from your previous accountant. Tell iComply these details when you enquire so the introduction is useful from the start.
